The juvenile and trafficking matters listed separately are outside ordinary adult scope and are carried as stop conditions.

Three of counsel's release blockers are answered by that text and the corrections are recorded on the affected tracks with provenance rather than silently applied: (1) SDCL 23A-3-34 says 'after five years', confirming counsel's five-year reading against the ten-year outlier; (2) SDCL 23A-27-17 says a court 'shall order' sealing upon discharge and dismissal, so SIS sealing is automatic and no participant motion exists, which removes the official_pdf_fill fallback counsel had left unresolved; (3) SDCL 23-6-8.1 says the director 'may authorize' destruction, so it is discretionary and bureau-initiated with nothing for a participant to file. Session-law provenance was also corrected: 23A-3-34 is SL 2016 ch 134 as amended by SL 2021 ch 106, not the 'SB174 (2021)' / June 2016 attribution in the review. effectiveFrom records the date each section's current operative text took effect; where the session law states no effective date the South Dakota default of July 1 following passage is applied, which is recorded as a nonblocking question on each affected track.

tracks.legalName: Motion for Expungement of Arrest Record (SDCL §§ 23A-3-26 to 23A-3-32)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a South Dakota arrest record

controllingAuthority.summary: An arrested person may apply to the court that would have jurisdiction over the crime for which the person was arrested for an order expunging the record of the arrest: after one year from the arrest where no accusatory instrument was filed; after one year from the date the prosecuting attorney formally dismisses the entire criminal case on the record; at any time after an acquittal; or within one year of a formal dismissal of the entire case on a showing of compelling necessity. The motion starts a new civil action, may be made only on a record of arrest, and more than one arrest record requires a separate case for each. The court may enter the order only after finding by clear and convincing evidence that the ends of justice and the best interests of the public and the defendant or arrested person will be served. Expungement in South Dakota means sealing, not destruction, and a nonpublic disposition record is retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation.

exclusions: Partial dismissals. Both the statute and the review turn on the ENTIRE criminal case being formally dismissed on the record; where some counts were dismissed and others resolved otherwise, this track is unavailable.
Convictions of any kind, which this track does not reach; South Dakota is not a broad adult conviction-expungement state.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records, which South Dakota relief does not reach.
More than one arrest record in a single filing; each arrest record requires its own civil action and its own fee.

units.label: Disposition classification, timing analysis and arrest-record count
units.description: The judgment stage, and the one that decides whether anything can be filed at all. Establish the correct court and county; establish whether the entire criminal case was formally dismissed on the record rather than partially; establish which of the four § 23A-3-27 timing branches applies and whether its clock has run; and count how many separate arrest records are involved, because each one requires its own civil action and its own $72 fee. The participant is directed to obtain the dismissal order, the acquittal judgment or proof that no accusatory instrument was filed, plus the court docket and a DCI criminal history. Nothing is filed at this stage and LegalEase does not receive, inspect or authenticate any of those records.

units.label: UJS motion packet: UJS-232, UJS-391 and the proposed UJS-394 order
units.description: The document stage. The South Dakota Unified Judicial System publishes a complete statewide form set, so the document work is form-fill and no custom pleading is advisable. LegalEase completes UJS-232 Case Filing Statement, UJS-391 Motion for Expungement and Statement of Mailing, and the proposed UJS-394 Order for Expungement which the judge signs. UJS-392 Waiver of Hearing is prepared conditionally, only where the arrested person, the prosecutor and any victim will all waive. UJS-393 Notice of Hearing is prepared conditionally where a hearing is required. The forms are identified by number and use but were not supplied in the archive; acquiring the current revisions is carried as a legal-design blocker on this track.

units.label: Filing, fee or indigency request, service on the State's Attorney, hearing or waiver, and UJS-395
units.description: The procedural stage, which runs after the packet exists and continues after the judge signs. File the new civil action with the clerk and pay the $72 civil filing fee or request indigency relief; mail or serve the State's Attorney, who may contest; serve any notice of hearing at least fourteen days before the hearing; coordinate the three-party waiver where all of the person, the prosecutor and any victim agree; and after the order is signed prepare and file UJS-395 Notice of Entry of Order and mail it with the order to the State's Attorney. This stage is guidance because its substance is timing, service and coordination with parties the participant does not control, not document production.

geography.venue: The court that would have jurisdiction over the crime for which the person was arrested. South Dakota is a unified judicial system with one statewide form set and no county variation.

destination.name: Clerk of Courts for the court with jurisdiction over the arrest or underlying case
destination.detail: The motion starts a new civil action filed with the clerk in the county of the arrest or underlying case. Pay the $72 civil filing fee or request an indigency waiver. Serve the State's Attorney, who may contest. More than one arrest record means more than one civil action.

rules.filing: The motion starts a NEW CIVIL ACTION filed with the Clerk of Courts in the court that would have jurisdiction over the crime for which the person was arrested. File UJS-232 and UJS-391 with the proposed UJS-394 order. More than one arrest record requires a separate civil action for each.
rules.fees: $72 civil filing fee per petition, per the current UJS instructions. The statute frames it as the same as the civil filing fee.
rules.feeWaiver: Available on a finding of indigency. The participant requests it from the court.
rules.notice: The State's Attorney is served and may contest. A hearing may be set unless waived by the arrested person or defendant, the prosecutor AND any victim — all three must waive. Any notice of hearing is served at least 14 days before the hearing. The court may require affidavits, testimony or other evidence, and may enter the order only after finding by clear and convincing evidence that the ends of justice and the best interests of the public and the person will be served.
rules.service: Serve or mail the motion to the prosecuting attorney and complete the Statement of Mailing on UJS-391. After the order is signed, file UJS-395 Notice of Entry of Order and mail it with the order to the State's Attorney.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs UJS-391. The prosecutor and any victim sign UJS-392 where the hearing is waived.

Prosecutor opposition, or any contested hearing.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of Record on Completion of a Diversion Program (SDCL §§ 23A-3-35 to 23A-3-37)
tracks.publicName: Clear a record after completing a diversion program

controllingAuthority.summary: A person placed in a diversion program is eligible for expungement of the entire criminal record related to that arrest if they successfully completed all the terms of the program and have not been charged with any new crimes, except petty offences or minor traffic citations, within one year and thirty days from the date of successful completion. Where those requirements are met the State's Attorney shall file a dismissal of all charges related to the arrest and a notice of completion of the diversion program, and upon that filing the court shall grant the expungement without the filing of a motion or any further action by the court.

exclusions: Any new crime charged within one year and thirty days from successful completion, other than petty offences or minor traffic citations.
Incomplete diversion, or any term of the diversion programme not satisfied.
Anything short of the ENTIRE criminal record related to that arrest; the statute is framed around the entire record.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Removal of Non-Felony Charges or Convictions from the Public Record (SDCL § 23A-3-34)
tracks.publicName: Automatic removal of a minor case from your public record

controllingAuthority.summary: Any charge or conviction resulting from a case where a petty offense, municipal ordinance violation or a Class 2 misdemeanor was the highest charged offense shall be automatically removed from a defendant's public record after five years if all court-ordered conditions on the case have been satisfied and the defendant has not been convicted of any further offenses within those five years. The case record remains available to court personnel or as authorized by order of the court and may be used as an enhancement in the prosecution of subsequent offenses as provided by law.

exclusions: Any case where the highest charged offense exceeded a Class 2 misdemeanor.
Any case with court-ordered conditions that have not been satisfied.
Any defendant convicted of a further offense within the five-year period.
Removal from the public record does not remove the record from court personnel, from access by order of the court, or from use as an enhancement in a later prosecution.

waitingPeriods.condition: Highest charged offense was a petty offense, municipal ordinance violation or Class 2 misdemeanor, all court-ordered conditions satisfied, and no further convictions in the period

destination.name: Operation of SDCL § 23A-3-34
destination.detail: Removal from the public record happens automatically once the five-year period runs and the conditions are met. There is no application, no motion and no fee. The participant's task is to verify that removal has occurred and to understand what survives it.

components.notes: Establish the highest charged offense in the case, whether all court-ordered conditions were satisfied, whether any further conviction occurred in the five years, and when the five-year period ran.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of Records on Discharge and Dismissal after a Suspended Imposition of Sentence (SDCL §§ 23A-27-13 to 23A-27-17)
tracks.publicName: Seal a record after a suspended imposition of sentence

controllingAuthority.summary: For certain offenses a court may suspend imposition of sentence where the person has never before been convicted of a felony. After the person completes all court conditions the defendant is discharged and the case is dismissed without adjudication of guilt, and the discharge and dismissal are not deemed a conviction for disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law. Upon the discharge and dismissal a court SHALL order that all official records, other than the nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation, be sealed along with all records relating to the arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, and dismissal and discharge. The order restores the person to the status occupied before arrest, indictment or information, and the person is not guilty of perjury or of giving a false statement for failing to recite or acknowledge the matter.

exclusions: Any person previously convicted of a felony, who is not eligible for a felony suspended imposition of sentence in the first place.
A second felony suspended imposition of sentence; the statute permits one felony SIS and one misdemeanor SIS per person.
Any case where the court conditions have not been completed and the discharge and dismissal have not issued.
The nonpublic records retained by the Division of Criminal Investigation, which are expressly excluded from the sealing order.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Sealing of Records on the Grant of a Chapter 24-14 Pardon (SDCL § 24-14-11)
tracks.publicName: Records sealed after a governor's pardon

controllingAuthority.summary: A person granted a pardon under the provisions of chapter 24-14 is released from all disabilities consequent on the conviction. Upon the granting of such a pardon the Governor shall order that all official records relating to the pardoned person's arrest, indictment or information, trial, finding of guilt, application for a pardon, and the proceedings of the Board of Pardons and Paroles be sealed. The Governor files a public document with the secretary of state certifying the pardon; that document remains public for five years and is then sealed. A pardon granted without following the provisions of the chapter may not be sealed. The pardon restores the person to their pre-arrest status and protects against perjury or false-statement liability for failing to acknowledge the matter, but the conviction may still be considered for sentencing on subsequent offences and habitual-offender determinations.

exclusions: Any pardon granted without following the provisions of chapter 24-14, which expressly may not be sealed.
The pardon application itself, which is a Board of Pardons and Paroles process requiring advocacy and is outside LegalEase self-help scope.
Federal, tribal, military and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Deferred Imposition of Sentence and Dismissal for Certain Controlled-Substance Offences (SDCL § 23A-27-53)

controllingAuthority.summary: After receiving a plea of guilty for a violation of § 22-42-5 or § 22-42-5.1 a court may, without entering a judgment of guilt and with the consent of the defendant, defer imposition of sentence and place the defendant on probation on terms that must include a drug and alcohol evaluation and any recommended course of treatment. If after one year the defendant has completed treatment and complied with all conditions, the court shall dismiss the § 22-42-5 or § 22-42-5.1 charge upon the defendant pleading guilty to ingestion under § 22-42-15 or possession under § 22-42-15.1. No person previously granted a deferred imposition of sentence is eligible for a second. A defendant is ineligible where aggravating circumstances exist as defined by § 22-6-11, or where the defendant is serving a sentence under the supervision of the executive branch.

exclusions: Any person previously granted a deferred imposition of sentence, who is ineligible for a second.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Counsel flagged as a release blocker whether § 23-6-8.1 destruction is automatic, discretionary or on request, because it determines whether there is anything for a participant to do. The section has now been read at the official South Dakota Legislature publication: the director of the Bureau of Criminal Statistics 'may authorize' the destruction. It is discretionary and bureau-initiated, and the section describes no participant application, petition or request. The section also covers three categories the review did not carry: deceased persons, persons seventy-five or older absent a violation in the last ten years, and incidents no longer considered crimes.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Additional research required, as counsel decided. Reading § 23-6-8.1 at the official source answers counsel's question about whether destruction is automatic, discretionary or on request — the director 'may authorize' it, so it is discretionary and bureau-initiated with no participant application described — and it widens the section beyond the misdemeanor branch the review carried. What remains open is how bureau destruction interacts with the DCI nonpublic record expressly retained on the expungement and SIS tracks, and whether there is any participant-facing action at all. The track is deferred, absent from runtime resolution and unreachable, with counsel's structure preserved and the statutory correction recorded.
